title: Capacity & Headroom Forecasting - Scaling Input Sheet (draft)
content:
PURPOSE:
This working sheet captures month-level inputs that feed the Optimize cost model. Focus is on forecasting demand (QPS and token mix), calculating safe headroom for SLOs, and converting into GPU-hours and monthly infra cost. Use this as the single source for scenario runs (baseline / high-growth / reserved-capacity).

SUMMARY OF SHEET LAYOUT (tab names):
- Inputs (this tab): baseline assumptions, per-model compute factors, GPU profiles
- Monthly-forecast: month-by-month QPS, median seq len, peak concurrency, enterprise add-ons
- Sizing: derived GPU-hours, required GPUs, reserved vs burst split
- Cost: cost per GPU-hour, reserved discounts, networking/storage
- Scenarios: baseline / +25% growth / enterprise surge (one-off)

KEY ASSUMPTIONS (inputs):
- GPU throughput (tokens/sec) per model class: small: 25k tps, medium: 12k tps, large: 3.5k tps
- Compute factor per token (relative kernel cost): small=0.6, medium=1.0, large=3.2
- Average tokens per request = median_seq_len * 1.05 (accounts for system tokens + metadata)
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for hosted; dedicated SLOs vary
- Headroom multiplier: baseline 1.3 (30% slack for bursts), enterprise-critical 1.6
- Batch efficiency: estimated improvement factor (tokens/sec) increases with batch but constrained by latency SLO
- Reserve discount: 30% off public hourly rate for annual commit

EXAMPLE MONTHLY-FORECAST ROW (verbatim cell-like text):
Month | ModelClass | ForecastedQPS | MedianSeqLen | AvgTokensPerReq | PeakMultiplier | PeakQPS | TargetP95 | HeadroomFactor | EffectiveQPSForSizing | Notes
2025-02 | medium | 350 | 256 | =256*1.05 -> 268.8 | 3.0 | 1050 | 200ms | 1.30 | =1050*1.3 -> 1365 | converted from product telemetry + 15% marketing campaign

DERIVED SIZING FORMULAE (human-readable):
- AvgTokens/sec at peak = PeakQPS * AvgTokensPerReq
- EffectiveComputeTokens = AvgTokens/sec * ComputeFactor (model class)
- GPU_throughput_effective = GPU_tokens_per_sec * BatchEfficiencyFactor
- Required_GPU_count (concurrent) = ceil( EffectiveComputeTokens / (GPU_throughput_effective / HeadroomFactor) )
- Monthly_GPU_hours = Required_GPU_count * 24 * days_in_month * utilization_factor (utilization_factor default 0.85 for hosted, 0.95 for dedicated)
- Monthly_infra_cost = Monthly_GPU_hours * price_per_GPU_hour * (1 - reserved_discount_if_applicable) + networking/storage estimates

NUMERIC EXAMPLE (from the 2025-02 row):
- PeakQPS = 1050 requests/s, AvgTokensPerReq = 269 -> tokens/sec = 282,450 tps
- ComputeFactor (medium) = 1.0 -> EffectiveComputeTokens = 282,450
- GPU_tokens/sec baseline (A100-like) = 12,000 tps / sec (assumption for medium profile); BatchEfficiencyFactor=1.6 at 40ms latency -> GPU_throughput_effective = 19,200
- HeadroomFactor=1.3 -> adjusted GPU throughput for sizing = 19,200 / 1.3 = 14,769
- Required GPUs concurrent = ceil(282,450 / 14,769) = ceil(19.13) -> 20 GPUs
- Monthly_GPU_hours (28 days) = 20 * 24 * 28 * 0.85 = 11,424 GPU-hours
- Price_per_GPU_hour (on-demand) = $3.20 -> infra cost = 11,424 * 3.2 = $36,556; with 30% reserved discount = $25,589

SCENARIO BREAKDOWN (short bullets):
- Baseline: use headroom 1.3, utilization 0.85 — conservative for hosted API.
- Growth+25%: scale forecasted QPS and re-run sizing; observe non-linear GPU step-ups (discrete GPUs) and tail latency risk.
- Enterprise dedicated: headroom 1.6, utilization 0.95, aim for reserved capacity + burst buffer (20% of peak as burst)

NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS (items to resolve in next sync):
- Confirm GPU_tokens/sec baselines across hardware matrix (A10, A100, H100). Current sheet uses A100-like numbers; SRE can supply microbench results (OPT-542).
- Add per-tenant QoS: how to account for rate-limited enterprise tenants that take reserved shards?
- Should we model KV-cache hit rates separately (saves ~X tokens/sec in many serving patterns)?
- How to reflect model quantization plan (Q8 vs Q4 -> ~1.7-2.8x speedups) and where to apply regressions for quality monitoring.

RECOMMENDATIONS (practical next steps for Optimize product):
1) Short term (2 weeks): lock compute factor table with Applied-ML (Jordan) and run microbench with H100, A100, A10. Owner: Jordan Liu.
2) Medium (1 month): update sheet to include cache hit assumptions per workload and add a toggle for quantization profile; add per-model SLA tiers. Owner: Ravi Shah.
3) Product change (Q1): expose a policy knob in console for "reserved vs burst split" and compute cost delta live in pricing estimator. Owner: Marta Gonzalez + Console eng.
4) Cost ops (30 days): produce a 'recommended reserve' signal (n GPUs) based on 90th-percentile monthly highs and publish as sales guidance for Dedicated customers. Owner: Finance & Solutions Eng.

ACTION ITEMS (linked):
- OPT-542: Microbench results for medium/large models (blocked by infra quota)
- OPT-560: Add quantization presets to Optimize recommendations (PR draft in github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pulls/34)

QUICK TODO (notes-to-self):
- add a small sensitivity table: cost vs headroom (1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.5) and vs batch-efficiency (1.1..2.0) -> visualize the convex cost surface
- check month-days formula for Feb/Leap-year handling in sheet macros

APPENDIX: Suggested columns for the 'Sizing' tab (flattened):
[month, model_class, peak_qps, median_seq_len, avg_tokens, compute_factor, batch_efficiency, gpu_tokens_per_sec, headroom, requisite_gpus, monthly_gpu_hours, utilization, price_per_gpu_hour, reserved_discount, monthly_cost_on_demand, monthly_cost_reserved, notes]

VERSION NOTES: draft v0.9 - still missing per-hardware microbench and KV-cache modeling.

LAST PARAGRAPH (context for reviewers):
This is intentionally a working sheet: keep edits inline and mark big assumption changes with a comment. When ready to finalize, we'll copy to a 'final' sheet with locked inputs and link from the Optimize product recommendations RFC.

END OF DOCUMENT
